# Payer escalation — claim never adjudicated

**Use when:** the claim was submitted and the payer has neither paid nor denied it.
Mailing a duplicate HCFA and waiting is not follow-up — escalate with a paper trail
and a deadline.

**Before sending:** run a 276/277 claim-status inquiry. If the payer has no record,
this becomes a timely-filing-protected resubmission, not an escalation.

---

[PRACTICE NAME] · NPI [GROUP NPI] · TIN [EIN]
[DATE] — **SECOND REQUEST**

[PAYER NAME], Provider Relations
[ADDRESS]

**RE: Failure to adjudicate — request for immediate processing**
Member: [NAME] · ID: [MEMBER ID] · Group: [GROUP]
Date of service: [DOS] · Billed: $[AMOUNT] · CPT: [CODES]
Original submission: [DATE] via [CLEARINGHOUSE] · Payer claim #: [IF KNOWN]

To Whom It May Concern:

The above claim was submitted on [DATE] and remains unadjudicated after
[N] days. We have received neither payment nor a remittance advice. A duplicate
CMS-1500 with cover letter was mailed on [DATE] and has also gone unanswered.

Proof of timely submission is enclosed ([clearinghouse acceptance report / 277CA]).
Because the delay is attributable to the payer, we consider timely filing satisfied
as of the original submission date.

**We request within 30 days:** adjudication of this claim, or written explanation of
the specific deficiency preventing it.

Absent a response we will [escalate to the plan's provider grievance process / file a
complaint with the NY State Department of Financial Services under the Prompt Pay Law,
Ins. Law § 3224-a, which requires payment or denial within 30 days of an electronic
clean claim, with interest accruing thereafter].

Respectfully,
[NAME], [TITLE] · [PHONE] · [EMAIL]

> **NY Prompt Pay:** § 3224-a requires payment or denial within 30 days (electronic) /
> 45 days (paper) of a clean claim, with interest at 12% annually. Citing it materially
> changes response rates. Verify current thresholds before sending.
